concepts.preferred_label: Congenital Heart Disease with Single Ventricle Defect
concepts.why: The patient has a known complex congenital heart disease with a single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with left superior vena cava.
The patient experiences occasional cyanosis, which is a common symptom of congenital heart disease.
The patient became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage during the pulmonary artery banding procedure.
The patient developed clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions, which are indicative of seizure activity.
The patient's head CT showed a slight diffuse increase in cortical density, which is consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
The patient has a low oxygen saturation and is taking furosemide and spironolactone, which are medications commonly used to treat cardiac failure.

rationales.F07: Oxygen saturation of 80% is a moderate indicator of Congenital Heart Disease with Single Ventricle Defect and a strong indicator of Cyanosis.
rationales.F10: Cardiorespiratory arrest is a strong indicator of Cardiorespiratory Arrest and Congenital Heart Disease with Single Ventricle Defect.
rationales.F11: Clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions are strong indicators of Seizure Disorder.
rationales.F12: A slight diffuse increase in cortical density is a strong indicator of Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
